# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: You have the manual. You can hear me, but you cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures (I only receive blanks). Therefore, you cannot tell me directly which wire to cut. You must use Deaf as your voice to reach me! Deaf can see your gestures, and Deaf can speak aloud for me to hear. Please gesture to Deaf to speak aloud everything visible on the bomb (display, light, wires). Once you find the solution in the manual, gesture the wire number to Deaf, and have Deaf speak aloud which wire to cut (e.g. 'Cut wire N'). As soon as Deaf speaks the command, I will cut it.

I cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. Furthermore, no convention has been established yet with Deaf for what specific gestures mean ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). 

Blind has already spoken. Deaf is next in the turn order. Deaf can see the bomb and can speak aloud so both Blind and I can hear. Deaf will describe the bomb's light and wires and can establish a gesture code for me to indicate the correct wire. Once Deaf describes the light and wires, I will look up the solution in the defusal manual and signal Deaf using the agreed gestures.

For now, I will wait for Deaf's turn.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Indicator light is yellow. Five wires: Wire 1 is green, Wire 2 is white, Wire 3 is red, Wire 4 is yellow, Wire 5 is blue.
Blind says to Mute: I heard Deaf: Display 0, yellow light, 1:green, 2:white, 3:red, 4:yellow, 5:blue. Consult the manual and gesture to Deaf which wire to cut, instructing Deaf to say it aloud. I am standing by to cut the wire Deaf names.

Based on the defusal manual, with a **yellow** indicator light, the wire to cut is the **red** wire.
Deaf reported that **Wire 3** is red.
I will gesture three index fingers (`☝ ☝ ☝`) to Deaf so Deaf knows to instruct Blind to cut Wire 3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb has changed after the correct cut. Since Deaf goes after me in the turn order (Blind, Mute, Deaf), Deaf has not yet had a chance to report the new state of the bomb. I need to wait for Deaf's turn so Deaf can describe the updated bomb status.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Wire 3 was cut. Indicator light is now green. Display shows 0. Remaining wires: Wire 1 is white, Wire 2 is yellow, Wire 3 is CUT, Wire 4 is blue, Wire 5 is green.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reported the indicator light turned GREEN. If the bomb is defused, we do nothing. If another wire needs to be cut, gesture the number to Deaf to have Deaf speak it to me.

Based on the manual, when the indicator light is **green**, the required wire color to cut is **green**.
Deaf reported that Wire 5 is green.
Following the previous convention where 3 index finger gestures signaled Wire 3, I will signal 5 index finger gestures to Deaf to indicate Wire 5.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The wire was cut correctly and the bomb has updated. I must wait for Deaf to observe and announce the new bomb status.


Blind says to Mute: Deaf reported indicator light turned WHITE. Remaining uncut wires: 1 is yellow, 2 is blue, 4 is white. Consult manual and gesture the next cut to Deaf to speak aloud.

The indicator light is white. According to the manual, when the light is white, the wire to cut is yellow.
Deaf reported that Wire 1 is yellow.
I will gesture 1 index finger to Deaf to indicate Wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Deaf reported indicator light turned RED. Uncut wires: Wire 2 is white, Wire 4 is blue. Consult manual and gesture the next cut to Deaf to speak aloud.

Based on the manual, when the indicator light is red, the wire to cut is blue.
Deaf reported that Wire 4 is blue.
I will gesture 4 index fingers to Deaf to indicate Wire 4.
